summary: Discovery for TempestFlow's streaming chatbot and event-driven classification pipelines. Main goals: p95 latency SLOs, concurrency strategy during marketing bursts, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and token/sec benchmarks. Agreed next steps: share pricing & benchmark script, customer to provide traffic samples, schedule a live mini-benchmark.
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick roll call?
00:12 Maya Lopez: Hi it's Maya, CTO at TempestFlow, thanks.
00:15 Jared Kim: Jared here, ML eng, focused on inference.
00:18 Riya Anand: Riya Platform/DevOps.
00:20 Nitin Rao: Nitin, Product.
00:22 Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood, I look after performance/benchmarks.
00:30 Alex: Awesome. The agenda real quick: p95 targets, your peak concurrency patterns, streaming vs sync calls, and then tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
00:45 Maya: Cool, I'll start with context. TempestFlow runs a customer-support assistant that's event-driven — chat + webhook triggers — we also run a near-realtime labeling pipeline that classifies short form user messages. Expected production qps right now is modest but we have big bursts during campaigns, like up to 1.2k concurrent sessions for short periods.
01:05 Jared: For inference model we use a 13B family open model, quantized fp16 sometimes, and we want streaming outputs to drive UI latency. Our p95 target is 350ms for streaming first-token and <1s for completion for most short replies (~60-120 tokens).
01:25 Alex: Okay good, that's specific. When you say streaming first-token p95 350ms, is that end-to-end client-to-first-chunk or server-side only?
01:34 Maya: Server-side only, we accept client network variance.
01:37 Samir: Got it. Couple clarifying Qs: what's your typical token length distribution during peaks? You mentioned 60-120 tokens — is that median?
01:47 Jared: Median around 40 tokens; upper tail 120ish. But we also have long-form support threads occasionally up to 800 tokens, but those are rare.
01:58 Riya: The bursts are short lived, 5-12 minutes during a campaign kickoff. We need graceful degradation — if we can't keep p95, fall back to a smaller model or queued responses.
02:10 Alex: Right. So high-level tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, Dedicated gives predictability for burst SLOs, Private brings network isolation + KMS control. For your use case, Dedicated with autoscale + burst pools often matches these campaign spikes.
02:30 Maya: Cost is a hard constraint — we run forecasts and marketing only funds some bursts. We'll need a model for unit cost per token and per-peak-minute. Do you have burst pricing?
02:41 Alex: Yes, we have burst add-on options on Dedicated and configurable burst on Hosted with higher compute rates during surge. We'll include a worked example per your traffic.
02:52 Samir: On technical side, two levers: batching and prefix/KV caching. For streaming with low latency you usually want minimal batching for first-token. We can keep micro-batches for later tokens and KV cache for multi-turn.
03:10 Jared: How does Redwood handle KV cache warmup across cold nodes during a burst? Our sessions are sticky-ish but not guaranteed.
03:20 Samir: Good question. We support automatic KV cache sharding and we can pre-warm caches based on session IDs if you provide routing keys. For Dedicated we can reserve cache lanes to reduce warmup. There's still a residual cold-start for new pods.
03:36 Riya: We run in GCP us-central predominantly, and we need a VPC option for the private deployment if we go that way. Also we need HSM-backed KMS for keys used with PII.
03:46 Alex: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share the integration notes — Samir will attach the KMS playbook.
03:54 Maya: On latency numbers, what's realistic for a 13B quantized model on your Dedicated tier w/ streaming enabled?
04:02 Samir: Rough ballpark: first-token p95 around 150-300ms depending on sequence length and hardware (A10s vs H100s). Completion p95 for 60-120 tokens on optimized kernels ~700ms to 1.2s. We'll need to run your exact workload to be sure.
04:23 Jared: Those first-token numbers look promising. What about concurrency per GPU? We saw in-house that with continuous batching we could get better throughput but at cost of higher tail if you wait to batch.
04:36 Samir: Exactly. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and adaptive batching thresholds. For user-facing streaming you often tune a smaller batch size and rely on more replicas. We'll provide guidance for tokens/sec per GPU at different batch profiles.
04:52 Nitin: Our business requirement: during a campaign we must keep 95% of user interactions ⩾ baseline experience, otherwise product ops flips to queued fallback. So we need deterministic capacity planning.
05:05 Alex: Understood. We can run a mini-benchmark: we host a transient Dedicated pool configured to mimic your peak, run your sample prompts, measure first-token p95 and completion p95, and produce an actionable capacity table (GPUs needed per concurrency level).
05:20 Maya: Timeline?
05:22 Alex: If you send prompts and traffic CSV by Fri (2029-09-26) we can run a benchmark early next week and share results.
05:30 Riya: We'll also need audit logs retained for 13 months and per-request metadata for debugging. Is that configurable?
05:38 Samir: Yes — Redwood Console supports per-route tracing and metadata retention; retention window and storage tier are configurable (and add-on). We'll include that in the security doc.
05:46 Maya: Any caveats with streaming and function/tool-calls? We call external tools from the model results sometimes. Latency compounds.
05:55 Samir: For tool-calls we recommend async invocation: stream partial content, then call tool, then stream resumed content. But if tool latencies are high you'll see end-to-end impact. You can also configure automatic fallback to cached answers for common tool outputs.
06:12 Jared: For benchmarks, can we test hosted vs. dedicated with identical model binary to compare? Model version pinning is important for us.
06:20 Alex: Yes, model pinning is supported; we can run identical containers across Hosted and Dedicated to measure pure infra differences. For Private (VPC/on-prem) the variability increases depending on networking.
06:31 Riya: Security: we need SAML SSO and RBAC to restrict who can start Dedicated pools.
06:37 Alex: SAML + SCIM and fine-grained RBAC are available on enterprise tiers. We'll include that in the security packet.
06:45 Maya: Competitors: we've looked at Anthropic for model quality and Pinecone for vector ops, but we like Redwood's focus on runtime economics.
06:53 Nitin: Also curious about observability — how deep are your token-level logs? Can we slice by user/session and measure p95 per customer segment?
07:03 Samir: Yes we produce token-level timing breakdowns: model compute, kv-cache hit/miss, batching delay, and network. You can filter by route/model/session in the Console.
07:17 Jared: Do you support quantized kernels (int8/4-bit) and how stable are those for our open 13B family?
07:24 Samir: We support quantized paths; we also test each model for quality regressions and include quantization recommendations. For some models int8 yields minimal degradation, some need fp16. We'll run QA alongside throughput runs.
07:38 Alex: I want to capture a couple of concrete numbers to put in the follow-ups: what concurrency do you think 1 A10 or 1 H100 can support for 13B streaming with p95-first-token under 350ms? Samir, rough?
07:52 Samir: Roughly: on A10 you might expect ~30-60 concurrent streaming sessions for that p95; on H100 maybe 80-160 depending on heartbeats and prompt length. These are very workload dependent — hence the bench.
08:09 Maya: That range is useful. For our campaign spikes (1.2k concurrent) we'd need a cluster — say if H100 supports 120/session average then ~10 H100s plus buffer? That seems pricey.
08:23 Alex: That's where Dedicated burst pools and autoscaling come in — you only pay for burst minutes. Also model-level fallback: route overflow to a smaller faster model for degraded experience but cheaper.
08:36 Nitin: Do you provide estimated cost per 1k tokens at each tier?
08:41 Alex: We'll include a cost model with per-token and per-minute reserved capacity numbers, and a burst example for your 12-minute windows.
08:49 Jared: On the mini-benchmark, can we measure token/sec sustained and tokens/sec burst-to-steady? We want to know warmup slope.
08:58 Samir: Yes, we'll capture sustained tps, peak tps, and tail latencies during ramp up. We'll also show cache warmup curves.
09:10 Riya: Network wise, how much egress do you charge for Private? We have large artifact pull during model startup.
09:18 Alex: For Private deployments model artifacts are transferred once; egress charges depend on cloud region/bandwidth, we'll call that out.
09:25 Maya: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
09:28 Samir: A few: 1) batching tuning is a tradeoff vs tail; avoid large batch windows for first-token, 2) KV cache miss storms during node churn can spike latency — plan warmup, 3) for sub-second p95 you want predictable hardware (Dedicated/H100) and pinned model versions.
09:50 Speaker 4: (unlabeled) Quick interjection, do you have any SLA on fallback or error budgets?
09:55 Alex: Our Dedicated contracts can include SLA targets (uptime and latency ranges) and error budget policies. We'll propose options.
10:05 Maya: Let's talk about benchmarking payloads — I'll describe them now: we have three prompt classes: micro (10-30 tokens), standard (40-120 tokens), long-form (200-800 tokens). Micro drives the chat UI, standard is most common. We can provide 5000 sample prompts with timestamps.
10:23 Jared: We'll also include conversation turns for multi-turn KV cache tests.
10:29 Samir: Perfect. For the benchmark script we'll need realistic arrival patterns (poisson + correlated spikes), and we recommend including session stickiness ratio.
10:38 Riya: About session stickiness — we average 70% sticky, 30% new. During campaign spikes stickiness drops to ~50%.
10:46 Samir: Noted. That affects cache hit rate substantially. We'll simulate both sticky and non-sticky scenarios.
10:55 Alex: Any regulatory constraints for data residency?
10:58 Maya: EU data residency for a subset of customers, but majority in US. So multi-region routing might be needed.
11:06 Samir: We support region routing and can pin certain tenants to Private deployments if required.
11:12 Jared: A bit nitty: do you expose per-token timing in real time for our telemetry system? We want to capture first-byte and last-byte timestamps.
11:20 Samir: Yes, we emit granular timing that can be forwarded to your observability pipeline via webhooks or S3 exports.
11:28 Nitin: On security follow-up: we need a whitepaper on KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 artifacts, and an architecture sketch for Private VPC flow.
11:36 Alex: We'll assemble those and include an on-call escalation matrix for Dedicated customers.
11:41 Maya: Budget: we have a limited pilot budget. If the benchmark proves we can hit p95 with 6 H100-equivalents for the peak, would you do a short pilot pricing?
11:51 Alex: Yes, we can propose a pilot package with discounted burst minutes to validate. We'll quantify once we see the bench numbers.
12:00 Jared: One more question — do you support multiplexed streaming to reduce SSH connections? (laughs) I mean multiplexed channels to reduce per-session overhead.
12:08 Samir: We support persistent HTTP/2 streams and keepalives; multiplexing is handled at transport layer. It helps with connection churn but doesn't change model compute.
12:17 Riya: Great. I think that's most of it.
12:20 Alex: Okay recap — deliverables: pricing + burst options, security pack, benchmark script, schedule mini-benchmark once prompts/CSV received.
12:30 Maya: Sounds good. Thanks all.
12:33 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up.
12:36 (call ends)
